mainTopic: Why the details of the פר העלם דבר של צבור need their own extra source, a dispute between תנאים about how far one comparison reaches, and two parables from דבי רבי ישמעאל explaining why the תורה describes the community's bull more briefly than the bull of the כהן משיח.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of why the community's bull needs an extra source to teach that the יותרת and the two כליות are burned for it. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא from a ברייתא, and רב פפא answers that this is a dispute between תנאים. Two teachings of דבי רבי ישמעאל then use parables about a king to explain why the תורה describes the community's bull more briefly than the bull of the כהן משיח. Next the גמרא turns to our משנה's line about one improper placement and brings the dispute in מנחות between רבי מאיר and חכמים about a פיגול thought during only half the מתיר. ריש לקיש explains that רבי מאיר really holds that a person acts on his first intention, and he proves this from the wording of our משנה. רבי שמואל בר יצחק rereads the משנה so that it fits the חכמים. רבא and רב אשי defend that reading, and a challenge to them is answered by saying the משנה only copied the style of its earlier clause. Finally, a ברייתא is brought against ריש לקיש, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the diaphragm and kidneys need an extra source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why an extra source is needed. The יותרת and the two כליות are never written in the section about the community's bull itself, so without the extra source we would not apply them there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the diaphragm and the two kidneys are not written about that bull itself. So you might say the rule does not apply there. That is why the extra source teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from just before this passage. It explains why one more derivation is needed for the פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some parts of the sacrifice are written explicitly in the section about the community's bull, so it is easy to apply them there. The יותרת and the two כליות are only written in the section about the פר כהן משיח. We might have thought they cannot be carried over, so the extra source ("קא משמע לן") tells us they are.

keyTerms.meaning: The diaphragm, or the lobe of the liver, one of the fats burned on the מזבח
The two kidneys
In the section about that thing itself
It teaches us (we need the source to tell us this)

phrases.english: But the diaphragm and the two kidneys,
which are not written about it itself,
phrases.notes: "It" is the community's bull, the פר העלם דבר של צבור. These parts appear only in the section about the כהן משיח's bull.

phrases.english: I might say: no, they do not apply;
so it teaches us that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation from before this passage of why an extra derivation is not wasted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifying an extra source by showing what we would have wrongly thought without it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the יותרת and כליות are not written in the community bull's own section, they would not be burned for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra source teaches that the community's bull matches the כהן משיח's bull in this detail too.

steps.title: רב הונא challenges from a ברייתא that includes everything
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא. A ברייתא learns that the bull of יום הכפורים gets everything said in this section, all from one comparison. So why should the יותרת and כליות need a separate source?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן said to רב פפא: But a תנא taught that the bull of יום הכפורים is included for everything stated in the section!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges רב פפא's claim that an extra source is needed. He points to a ברייתא in which one comparison seems to cover every detail at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one comparison can carry over every detail of the section, then the יותרת and כליות should be carried over automatically. A separate extra source would be unnecessary, and that weakens the explanation in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: But a תנא taught (introducing a challenge from a ברייתא)
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
For everything said in this section

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:
But the tanna taught:
phrases.notes: This refers to a ברייתא that reads the words "to the bull" in ויקרא 4:20 as including other bulls.

phrases.english: the bull of Yom Kippur is included
for everything stated in the section, he says!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 1 that the יותרת and כליות need their own extra source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the יותרת and כליות need an additional derivation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that one comparison carries over every detail in the section, so a separate source for these parts would be unnecessary.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the תנאים disagree. The תנא of דבי רב lets one comparison cover everything. The תנא of דבי רבי ישמעאל does not, so in his view separate sources are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. The תנא of the school of רב includes everything this way. The תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל does not include this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by showing that the ברייתא follows a different view. רב פפא's explanation follows the other תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two approaches to how far one comparison reaches. One approach lets it carry over every detail. The other limits it, which is why רב פפא needed extra sources. The ברייתא and רב פפא simply follow different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The study hall of רב
Includes, extends the rule to more cases
In this way

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from the ברייתא is answered by splitting the views. דבי רב learns every detail from one comparison. דבי רבי ישמעאל needs separate sources, so רב פפא's extra derivation fits his view.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im;
the tanna of the school of Rav includes in this way,
phrases.notes: He means: one comparison is enough to carry over every detail.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לָא מְרַבֵּי הָכִי.
phrases.english: the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not include in this way.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים (the source follows a different opinion)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that one comparison covers all details, so the extra source would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only דבי רב holds that way. דבי רבי ישמעאל requires separate sources.

steps.title: Parable of the king who spoke little of his beloved's offense
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל explains why the יותרת and כליות are written for the bull of the כהן משיח but not for the community's bull. A king who loves someone does not dwell on that person's wrongdoing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Why are the diaphragm and two kidneys stated for the anointed priest's bull but not for the bull of the community's mistaken ruling? It is like a human king who was angry at someone he loved, and spoke little of his offense because of his love.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל. It gives a reason, through a parable, for why the תורה describes the community's bull more briefly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving details out of the community's bull is not an accident. The תורה keeps the description of כלל ישראל's sin offering short out of love for them, just as a king who loves someone keeps quiet about that person's offense. This fits with step 3: דבי רבי ישמעאל sees these missing details as meaningful.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for his mistaken sin
The bull brought when the community sins because of a mistaken ruling of the בית דין
A parable
His offense
His affection

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶאֶמְרוּ יוֹתֶרֶת וּשְׁתֵּי כְלָיוֹת
phrases.english: For what reason are the diaphragm and two kidneys stated
for the bull of the anointed priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּפַר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר?
phrases.english: and are not stated for the bull of the community's hidden matter?
phrases.notes: "Hidden matter" means a mistaken ruling of the court that led the whole community to sin.

phrases.english: A parable: to a king of flesh and blood
who was angry at his beloved,
and said little about his offense because of his affection.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: מִפְּנֵי מָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related aggadic teaching from the same school just mentioned in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה shortens its description of the community's sin offering out of love for כלל ישראל.

steps.title: Parable of the province that sinned
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל explains why "פרכת הקדש" (the curtain of holiness) is said for the bull of the כהן משיח, while the community's bull only says "the curtain." When most of a province sins against a king, his close relationship with his court does not stay the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל also taught: Why is "the curtain of holiness" said for the anointed priest's bull but not for the community's bull? It is like a human king whose province sinned against him. If a minority sinned, his entourage remains. If the majority sinned, his entourage does not remain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל. Again it uses a parable to explain a word that is missing in the community's bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one person sins, even the כהן משיח, the place stays fully "holy." When the whole community sins, it is like most of the province rebelling, so the relationship is damaged. That is why the word "holiness" is dropped there. This parable points the opposite way from step 4: there the missing words showed love, and here the missing word shows a harmed relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain of holiness, in front of the קודש הקדשים
A province
The king's entourage or court
Remains, stays as it was

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parables. In the first, leaving words out shows love. In the second, leaving out "holiness" shows that the sin of the many damages the relationship.
steps.whatToRemember: דבי רבי ישמעאל reads the differences between the כהן משיח's bull and the community's bull as meaningful. Fewer details show affection, and the missing "קדש" shows the weight of a sin of the many.

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For what reason is "the curtain of holiness" stated
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:6. For the community's bull, ויקרא 4:17 says only "the curtain."

phrases.english: for the bull of the anointed priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר בְּפַר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר?
phrases.english: and is not stated for the bull of the community's hidden matter?
A parable: to a king of flesh and blood
against whom a province sinned;
if a minority of it sinned,
his entourage remains,
if the majority of it sinned,
his entourage does not remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: מִפְּנֵי מָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel teaching from the same school about another wording difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word "holiness" is dropped for the community's bull because a sin of the majority damages the relationship with ה׳.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both parables explain wording differences between the two bulls as meaningful messages.

steps.title: A new discussion opens with a related משנה from מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה and brings a משנה from מנחות. There, רבי מאיר says a פיגול thought during only the קומץ or only the לבונה makes the offering פיגול with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said: 'Therefore, if he placed all of them properly, etc.' We learned in another משנה: if he had a פיגול thought during the קומץ but not the לבונה, or during the לבונה but not the קומץ, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and one who eats it gets כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic on our משנה's line about one improper placement. It brings a משנה from מנחות to set up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה has two parts that make it permitted: the קומץ (handful) and the לבונה (frankincense). רבי מאיר says a פיגול thought during just one of them is enough for full פיגול and כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the thought of eating or burning it after its proper time; one who eats it gets כרת
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense, burned together with the קומץ

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם נָתַן כּוּלָּן כְּתִיקְנָן כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Therefore, if he placed all of them in their proper manner, etc.
We learned there:
If he had a פיגול thought with the handful but not with the frankincense;
or with the frankincense but not with the handful –
Rabbi Meir says: it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The earlier discussion about the יותרת and כליות has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a פיגול thought during only the קומץ or only the לבונה makes the מנחה פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: חכמים require the thought during the whole מתיר
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. There is no כרת unless the פיגול thought was present during the entire מתיר, meaning both the קומץ and the לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: there is no כרת unless he has the פיגול thought during the whole permitting act.
steps.whatsHappening: The second side of the מנחות משנה is given. חכמים say that one part of the מתיר is not enough for כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the קומץ and לבונה together make up one מתיר, so the פיגול thought must cover both of them. This sets up the question of how רבי מאיר could disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The act or item that makes the offering permitted to eat or offer
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
There is no כרת for it
unless he makes the פיגול thought during the entire permitting act.
phrases.notes: The whole מתיר here means both the handful and the frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no כרת unless the פיגול thought covers the whole מתיר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש explains רבי מאיר: a person acts on his first intention
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רבי מאיר does not hold that half a מתיר can make פיגול. The case is one where the קומץ was offered with the bad thought and the לבונה was offered in silence. Since a person acts on his first intention, the לבונה also counts as offered with the bad thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Do not say רבי מאיר's reason is that half a מתיר can make פיגול. Rather, the case is where he offered the קומץ with the bad thought and the לבונה silently. רבי מאיר holds that anyone who does something does it with his first intention.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains רבי מאיר's view in a way that keeps the basic rule the same: the whole מתיר is still needed for פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר and חכמים agree that the פיגול thought must cover the whole מתיר. They argue only about the silent second part. רבי מאיר says it carries over the first intention, so the thought really did cover everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of the permitting act, such as only the קומץ or only the לבונה
In silence, without saying any specific intention
With his first intention
'What case are we dealing with here?': it narrows the case

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes רבי מאיר's argument from a dispute about half a מתיר into a dispute about whether a silent act continues the first intention.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Do not say that the reason of Rabbi Meir
is that he holds one can make פיגול with half a permitting act;
rather, what are we dealing with here?
For example, where he placed the handful with the bad thought,
and the frankincense in silence;
he holds: anyone who does something
does it with his first intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי מאיר's view from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's view applies when the bad thought came first and the second part was done silently. Everyone still agrees that half a מתיר alone cannot make פיגול.

steps.title: Proof from the wording of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where ריש לקיש learns this. It answers from our משנה: 'all properly and one improperly' is פסול without כרת. That suggests the reverse order, with the improper one first and the rest properly, is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From what our משנה teaches: 'If he placed all properly and one improperly, it is פסול and there is no כרת.' This implies that if one was improper first and all the rest were proper, it is פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where ריש לקיש's idea comes from. The order of the words in our משנה hints at the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts 'all properly' first, and in that order there is no כרת. So if the improper placement comes first, the later silent placements follow his first intention and the offering becomes פיגול. That matches ריש לקיש's 'first intention' reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where?': it asks for the source
In its proper manner
'But this': it draws an implied reverse case from the wording

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the order. 'All proper, then one improper' gives no כרת. 'One improper first, then all proper' gives פיגול, because the later acts follow his first intention.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that the משנה teaches:
Therefore, if he placed all of them in their proper manner
and one not in its proper manner,
it is disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.
This implies that if one was not in its proper manner
and all the rest were in their proper manner, it is פיגול;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ריש לקיש's explanation from step 8 by reading our משנה closely.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that a silent act follows the first intention
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the words in our משנה ('all properly and one improperly') implies the reverse order is פיגול.

steps.title: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote the line in our משנה. It rules out the חכמים and says it must be רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say the חכמים, they say there is no פיגול with half a מתיר! So it must be רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues ריש לקיש's proof from step 9. The גמרא figures out which opinion our משנה follows, so it can then show what that opinion's reasoning must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in step 9 was that 'one improperly first, then the rest properly' would be פיגול. But in that case only part of the service had the bad thought. The חכמים hold that half a מתיר never makes פיגול, so they could not agree. That leaves רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (whose opinion is this)
If you say
We make (an offering) פיגול
Half of the service that makes the offering permitted

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
phrases.notes: He means the inference from step 9: improper first, then the rest proper, would be פיגול.

phrases.english: If you say it is the Rabbis,
but the Rabbis say:
one cannot make piggul with half a permitting factor!
Rather, it is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof for ריש לקיש by naming the author of the משנה's implied ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion, רבי מאיר or the חכמים, our משנה follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר, because the חכמים don't allow פיגול with half a מתיר.

steps.title: So רבי מאיר's reason must be 'first intention'
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר's reason were just 'half a מתיר makes פיגול,' the משנה's case would be פיגול too. So his reason must be that a person acts on his first intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבי מאיר's reason is that half a מתיר makes פיגול, then even the case the משנה teaches should be פיגול! Isn't it rather because he holds that anyone who acts, acts on his first intention?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's proof. It shows that רבי מאיר's reason must be 'a person acts on his first intention,' exactly as ריש לקיש said in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case (proper first, one improper last) there is still a bad thought on part of the service. Yet the משנה says no כרת. So 'half a מתיר' cannot be רבי מאיר's reason. The difference must be the order: whatever the כהן intended at the start carries over to the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in the משנה)
He holds
He acts on his first intention

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's proof: our משנה follows רבי מאיר, and his reason is 'first intention,' not 'half a מתיר.'

phrases.english: And if Rabbi Meir's reason
is because one makes piggul with half a permitting factor,
then even as it is taught, it should also be piggul!
phrases.notes: The משנה's case is all proper and only the last one improper. That is still a bad thought on part of the service.

phrases.english: Is it not because he holds:
anyone who performs an action
performs it with his first intention?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם דִּמְפַגְּלִין בַּחֲצִי מַתִּיר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 10's identification of רבי מאיר to pin down his reasoning.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי מאיר's reason is על דעת ראשונה הוא עושה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: all properly and one improperly is פסול without כרת.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר יצחק: the משנה could be the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר יצחק says the משנה really follows the חכמים. He reads 'כתיקנן' as 'done the right way for פיגול,' meaning with a פיגול thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: Really it is the חכמים. And what does 'properly' mean? 'Properly' for פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא pushes back on ריש לקיש's proof. He offers a different reading of the משנה, so that it follows the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his reading, the first placements had a פיגול thought and the last one was done with no special thought. The משנה says there is no כרת. That fits the חכמים, who don't say the first intention carries over and don't allow פיגול with half a מתיר. So the proof for ריש לקיש falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually
In their proper manner
For פיגול (with a פיגול thought)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'proper' does NOT mean kosher. In this reading it means 'done the right way to make פיגול.' That flipped meaning is the whole point.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
Actually, it is the Rabbis;
and what does 'in their proper manner' mean?
In their proper manner for piggul.
phrases.notes: So the last placement, done 'not properly,' was simply done with no פיגול thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 9-11 by rereading the משנה's wording.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה must follow רבי מאיר and support ריש לקיש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed כתיקנן means kosher. It could mean 'with a פיגול thought.'

steps.title: The ruling 'פסול' shows that 'proper' means kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמואל בר יצחק. The משנה's 'therefore' clause shows that the one improper placement is what makes the offering פסול, so 'proper' must mean kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since it teaches: 'Therefore, if he placed all properly and one improperly, it is פסול and there is no כרת,' we learn that 'properly' comes to mean kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמואל בר יצחק's reading using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules the offering פסול, which shows that the one placement done 'not properly' is what disqualifies it. In רבי שמואל בר יצחק's reading, that last placement was done with no thought at all, and a placement like that disqualifies nothing. So 'properly' must mean kosher and 'not properly' must mean with a bad thought, and כתיקנן cannot mean 'with a פיגול thought.' The next step, from רבא, answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches
Therefore
By inference, we learn that
For making it kosher

phrases.english: But from the fact that it teaches:
Therefore, if he placed all of them in their proper manner
and one not in its proper manner,
it is disqualified and there is no karet;
we learn by inference that 'its proper manner'
comes to mean making it fit!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמואל בר יצחק's reading that כתיקנן means 'with a פיגול thought.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling פסול shows that the one improper placement is what disqualifies the offering. A silent placement could not do that, so 'proper' must mean kosher, not פיגול.

steps.title: רבא: the improper placement was a thought of eating outside the proper place
steps.stepSummary: רבא saves רבי שמואל בר יצחק's reading. 'שלא כתיקנה' means a thought of חוץ למקומו, and that thought ruins the פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'not in its proper way' mean? It means with a thought of eating the offering outside its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from step 13. He keeps 'כתיקנן' as 'with a פיגול thought' and explains the 'improper' placement as a different bad thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that the one improper placement must be what disqualifies, so 'proper' must mean kosher. רבא agrees that the improper placement is what disqualifies. In his reading, though, that placement had a חוץ למקומו thought, which spoils the offering without making it פיגול. So 'proper' can still mean 'with a פיגול thought,' and the משנה fits the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in its proper way; here, with a different kind of bad thought
Intending to eat the offering outside its proper area; this disqualifies but does not make פיגול

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is meant by 'not in its proper way'?
With a thought of eating it outside its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 and defends רבי שמואל בר יצחק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The improper placement disqualifies, so 'proper' must mean kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The improper placement had a חוץ למקומו thought. That disqualifies it, so 'proper' can still mean 'with a פיגול thought.'

steps.title: רב אשי: the improper placement was done not for its sake
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different explanation. 'שלא כתיקנה' means the placement was done שלא לשמו, which disqualifies a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'Not in its proper way' means 'not for its own sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another way to defend רבי שמואל בר יצחק. The improper thought was 'not for the sake of this offering.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא, רב אשי keeps 'proper' as 'with a פיגול thought.' He just names a different spoiling thought. For a חטאת, a שלא לשמו thought disqualifies the offering, so it cannot become פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake; done with a different offering in mind, which disqualifies a חַטָּאת

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It means 'not for its sake.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 13, parallel to רבא's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reinterpretation of the same term
steps.terutzMaskana: The improper placement was שלא לשמו, which disqualifies the offering and blocks פיגול.

steps.title: Then a silent last placement would make it פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to both answers. If the bad thought is what blocks פיגול, then a silent last placement would leave it פיגול, and the חכמים do not hold that.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he did not do it with a thought of 'outside its place' or 'not for its sake,' he would be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא and רב אשי. It points to an unwanted implication of their reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only thing stopping פיגול is the special bad thought on the last placement, then a last placement done with no thought at all would let the offering be פיגול. But the חכמים hold that a פיגול thought on only part of the מתיר cannot make פיגול. So the משנה would no longer match the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer that
He is liable, meaning כָּרֵת for eating פִּיגּוּל

steps.confusionAlert: The case being inferred is a last placement done silently, with no thought at all. It is not a case where the last placement was done with a פיגול thought.

phrases.english: This implies that when he does not do it
phrases.notes: This is talking about the last placement, done silently with no special thought.

phrases.english: with 'outside its place' or 'not for its sake'
he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּכִי לָא עָבֵיד לַהּ חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answers of רבא and רב אשי
steps.kashyaTarget: The readings of רבא and רב אשי as a way to fit the משנה to the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their reading implies a silent last placement leaves the offering פיגול, which contradicts the חכמים' view that half a מתיר cannot make פיגול.

steps.title: The wording just copies the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: The משנה wrote 'פסול ואין בו כרת' only to match its earlier clause, 'פיגול וחייבין עליו כרת.' No implication should be drawn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the earlier clause taught 'פיגול and one is liable for כרת,' the later clause also taught 'פסול and there is no כרת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 16. The משנה's phrasing is stylistic and should not be read for implications.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In truth, even a silent last placement would not make the offering פיגול according to the חכמים. The משנה described a case with a specific bad thought only so the later clause would match the style of the earlier one. So the inference from step 16 is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because (introduces wording chosen to match another clause)
The first clause
The later clause

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמואל בר יצחק's reading survives. The משנה can follow the חכמים, and its wording in the later clause simply mirrors the earlier clause.

phrases.english: Since it taught in the first clause
'פיגול, and one is liable for כרת for it,'
it also taught in the later clause
'disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's mention of a specific bad thought implies a silent placement would make פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording only matches the earlier clause. Even a silent placement would not make it פיגול.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge to ריש לקיש from a ברייתא that limits the rule to blood placed on the outer מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: When is this rule said? With blood placed on the outer מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against ריש לקיש. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the rest comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the rule of a פיגול thought on the first placement applies to blood placed on the outer מזבח, where one placement is enough to permit the offering. The limiting phrase 'במה דברים אמורים' hints that offerings needing several placements, like those on the inner מזבח, work differently. That would cut against ריש לקיש, and the next lines will show how.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (limits a rule to certain cases)
The outer altar in the courtyard

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
In what case is this said?
With blood that is placed on the outer altar;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the משנה's author and returns to challenging ריש לקיש's main rule
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation from step 8: a silent later act follows the first intention, so a פיגול thought in the first placement alone makes the offering פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the first-placement rule to the outer מזבח. The rest of the ברייתא will show this conflicts with ריש לקיש.
